newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Aziz meets U.N. chief arms inspector Butler.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Aziz meets U.N. chief arms inspector Butler.

text.p: United Nations arms envoy Richard Butler met Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz to discuss Baghdad's weapons of mass destruction, a U.N. official said on Wednesday.
Jo Lomas, special assistant to the head of Iraq's Ongoing Monitoring and Verification Centre (OMV), said Butler would meet Aziz again later on Wednesday.
"He had introductory talks with Mr Aziz," Lomas told Reuters in Baghdad.
Butler, who heads the United Nations Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of dismantling Iraq's prohibited weapons, began his first visit to Baghdad on Monday.
Butler told reporters shortly after his arrival that he hoped to be able to close Iraq's weapons file "as soon as possible".
Lomas said Butler, an Australian who took over from Sweden's Rolf Ekeus on July 1 as chairman of UNSCOM, on Tuesday inspected an Iraqi site which she declined to identify.
Butler is accompanied by his deputy Charles Duelfer and Russian ballistic missile expert Nikita Smidovich.
Iraqi media have urged Butler to open a new page with Baghdad.

UNSCOM must certify Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction before the United Nations will lift curbs imposed on Iraq's oil exports after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait, although Baghdad is allowed limited oil exports under a humanitarian deal.
